- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) or shows sharp decline, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price has recently fallen.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; apply a “cool-down” bias — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75–80), model often fails to recognize it; increase downward bias in forecast horizon.
- When sentiment and price history show divergence (e.g., sentiment bullish but price falling), model may misalign; prioritize sentiment over pure technical trend.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) — apply a “lag correction” by reducing forecast by 1–3% per day for first 7 days.
- If true outcome shows a sharp reversal after a high, model often fails to anticipate — add a “reversal buffer” to forecast, especially if sentiment shifts from bullish to neutral/negative.
